source.title: Some Open Problems Concerning the Convergence of Positive Series

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a general decision procedure or universal convergence criterion that, given an arbitrary series Σ a_n of nonnegative terms, determines whether the series converges or diverges? More broadly, is there any systematic structural pattern that decides convergence for positive series in general?

evidence.quote: Problem 1. What decides if a positive series is convergent or divergent ? Is there any universal convergence test? Is there any pattern in convergence?
Problem 2. Find an algorithm to determine whether a positive series is convergent or not.

accepted.question_text: Let ϕ: N → (0, ∞) be an increasing function with ϕ(n) → ∞, and define the weighted upper density of a set A ⊂ N by d̄_ϕ(A) = lim sup_{n→∞} |A ∩ [1, n]| / ϕ(n). If A has positive weighted upper density for the weight ϕ(n) = n / ln n, must the harmonic subseries Σ_{n∈A} 1/n diverge? More generally, must divergence still follow for the analogous weights n / [(ln n)(ln ln n) ···]?
accepted.context_brief: Weighted density versus harmonic subseries divergence

evidence.quote: Problem 3. Given an increasing function ϕ : N → (0, ∞ ) with limn→∞ ϕ (n) = ∞ , we define the upper density of weight ϕ by the formula ¯dϕ(A) = lim sup n→∞ |A ∩ [1, n ]| / ϕ (n) .

Does every subset A ⊂ N with ¯dn/ ln n(A) > 0 generate a divergent subseries ∑ n∈ A 1/n of the harmonic series? What about the case of other weights n/ [(ln n) (ln lnn) · · ·(ln ln · · ·ln n k times )]?

accepted.question_text: If A is a set of positive integers such that the reciprocal sum Σ_{n∈A} 1/n diverges, must A contain arithmetic progressions of arbitrarily large finite length? The source further notes that this remains open even in the special case of asking whether such a set must contain a 3 term arithmetic progression.
accepted.context_brief: Erdős conjecture on divergent reciprocal sets

evidence.quote: Conjecture 1. (P. Erd¨ os). If the sum of reciprocals of a set A of integers diverges, then that set contains arbitrarily long arithmetic progressions.
This conjecture is still open even if one only seeks a single progression of length three.
